source.author: verg
source.text: quantus ab occasu veniens pluvialibus Haedis verberat imber humum, quam multa grandine nimbi in vada praecipitant, cum Iuppiter horridus austris torquet aquosam hiemem et caelo cava nubila rumpit.
source.text_original: quantus ab occasu veniens pluvialibus Haedis / verberat imber humum, quam multa grandine nimbi / in vada praecipitant, cum Iuppiter horridus austris / torquet aquosam hiemem et caelo cava nubila rumpit.
source.text_english: As great as the rain that, coming from the west, lashes the ground beneath the rainy Haedi, as the showers hurl down so much hail into the shallows, when grim Jupiter, with the south winds, twists the watery winter and tears the hollow clouds apart in the sky.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: imbrem et tenebras saevumque tridentem iam iam ego et inviti torsissem coniugis ignem.
reuse.text_original: imbrem et tenebras saevumque tridentem / iam iam ego et inviti torsissem coniugis ignem.
reuse.text_english: I myself would already now have hurled rain and darkness and the savage trident, and my wife’s fire, though unwillingly.
